Below are the four new files. Each directory gets its own copy; nothing is shared, so the same change must be made twice.

`dev/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  namespace: myapp
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`dev/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-access-dev
  namespace: myapp
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-access-dev
  description: Read/write access to the myapp-logs-dev bucket only
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "LogsObjectAccess",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

`prod/logs-bucket.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  namespace: myapp
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  versioning:
    status: Enabled
  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true
```

`prod/logs-policy.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-access-prod
  namespace: myapp
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-access-prod
  description: Read/write access to the myapp-logs-prod bucket only
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "LogsObjectAccess",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:PutObject"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-prod/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

Each policy document names only the logs bucket, so the existing assets-bucket grant in `iam.yaml` is untouched and not widened.

## Attaching the policies

A standalone ACK `Policy` is not attached to anything by itself. Add a reference to it in the existing principal in each directory's `iam.yaml` — again, once per directory:

In `dev/iam.yaml`, on the `User` resource, add the new policy to its reference list alongside the existing app policy:

```yaml
spec:
  # ...existing fields unchanged...
  policyRefs:
    # ...existing entry for the assets policy stays as-is...
    - from:
        name: myapp-logs-access-dev
```

In `prod/iam.yaml`, the same edit on the `Role` resource:

```yaml
spec:
  # ...existing fields unchanged...
  policyRefs:
    # ...existing entry for the assets policy stays as-is...
    - from:
        name: myapp-logs-access-prod
```

If your ACK IAM controller version predates `policyRefs` and the existing `iam.yaml` instead lists concrete ARNs under `policies:`, append the corresponding ARN there instead (`arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:policy/myapp-logs-access-dev` / `...-prod`), keeping the existing entries.

Apply with the usual `kubectl apply -f dev/` and `kubectl apply -f prod/`. Since the two directories are fully independent, applying only `dev/` leaves prod entirely unchanged, and vice versa.
